Marissa,

We saw a significant spike starting ~08:45 PDT where the patient billing flow (checkout -> invoice generation) had repeated 500s and token-level latencies jumped from ~120ms to >2s. This impacted ~27% of requests for a period of ~18 minutes, and then saw intermittent errors afterward. Attached is a short log extract from our edge (cumulus_incident_log_excerpt.txt).

Our SRE (cc) opened an internal incident but asked us to loop you in for an RCA and mitigation timeline. This is high-impact for our billing window today; execs are monitoring.

Can Redwood confirm whether this correlates with any model/serving changes or capacity events on your side?

Asha

Quick triage summary (10:18 PDT):
- Observed a KV-cache miss storm concentrated on seq lengths ~512 tokens for a subset of t2 instances serving model "redwood-alpha-3".
- CPU utilization on the host level remained normal; GPU queue depth spiked causing increased scheduler latency and token emission delays.
- There was a transient scheduling policy flip related to a background rebalancer (rollout: 2026-09-14T07:50Z) that adjusted pod placement due to an unrelated autoscaler event in the same region. The rebalancer temporarily favored larger batch windows which increased tail latencies under this particular request shape.

Attachments: postmortem-slide-deck.pdf (draft) — contains charts for token latency distribution and timeline; kvcache_latency-snapshot.png included.

Immediate mitigations enacted (10:05 PDT):
- Rolled back the rebalancer behavior to prior conservative scheduling policy (hotfix) — observed latency drop within ~3m.
- Increased kv-cache reservation for the affected model class to reduce misses.
- Enabled per-customer request routing to avoid cross-tenant batch amplification for Cumulus for the next 6 hours.

Open items (needs follow-through):
1) Post-incident rule: add workload-aware guardrail to prevent rebalancer from switching batch-window policy for critical accounts during billing windows. Owner: Rishi. ETA: 2026-09-20.
2) Add additional telemetry: per-tenant token queue-depth and batch composition metrics. Owner: Jonas. ETA: 2026-09-24.
3) Evaluate longer-term: refine scheduling heuristics to minimize tail-latency impact for mid-length sequences. Owner: Research/Runtime (Kimberly to coordinate). ETA: 2026-10-08.

I'll fold these into the slide deck and share the 48-hour synthesis.

Rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Team — for the exec audience at Redwood and Cumulus, please see the tight summary below I floated on the bridge:

Executive synopsis (one-paragraph):
A transient scheduling policy change combined with KV-cache miss amplification produced a short-lived but high-impact tail-latency event during Cumulus Health's morning billing window. Immediate mitigations were effective and production latency returned to baseline. Root cause is an insufficient guardrail in the rebalancer logic that allowed larger batch windows to be selected for tenant mixes that include mid-length sequences.

Actionable asks for leadership:
- Approve a customer goodwill package (billing credit & 3-month elevated SL retention) for Cumulus — Finance input required. Owner: Grace.
- Prioritize the rebalancer guardrail as P1 in next week's runtime sprint and reserve 2 engineer-weeks. Owner: Kimberly.
- Schedule an executive readout with Cumulus on Friday (09/17) 14:00 PDT for a formal synthesis and Q&A. Owner: Marissa.

Please acknowledge owners and timelines; I'll prepare the one-pager for the CPO and the customer execs.

Jonas
VP, Customer Success (Ops Liaison)
